summary: SLA Suggester batch job misapplies low-priority overrides during DST window
description:
Issue summary:
The nightly 'sla-suggester' autoroute batch job applied low-priority SLA override macros to ~75 routing templates in prod us-east during the recent daylight saving time (DST) transition. The change reduced priority weights for several enterprise routing cohorts, causing delayed escalations and an increase in automatic autoreply routing for a subset of internal workflows.

Impact:
- Internal support escalation latencies increased by ~20% for affected cohorts between 2026-03-09 23:00 and 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC.
- No public customer-facing outages observed, but internal routing and SLA reporting were inconsistent.
- Affected templates: approx 75 routing macros across two routing namespaces (support-queue and ops-automation).

Environment:
prod | us-east
components: routing-engine, sla-orchestrator, autoroute-job, reporting-pipeline

Steps to reproduce (investigation reproduction):
1) Run sla-suggester with --simulate false against snapshot 2026-03-09T22:30Z in prod mirror.
2) Observe that time-window rules in macros that specify local wall-clock windows (e.g., \"23:00-02:00\") are normalized to UTC incorrectly when DST flag is set.
3) The suggester generates override patches that set priority_weight=-20 for affected macros and pushes them through the autoroute merger.

Observed behavior:
- The batch job interprets local rule windows using a DST offset conversion routine that double-applies the DST delta for rules crossing DST boundary, shifting windows by one extra hour. This made some macros appear as \"out-of-window\" to the simulator and the suggester applied conservative low-priority overrides.

Expected behavior:
- Time-window normalization should reliably map local wall-clock windows to UTC once per conversion without double-counting DST adjustments. The suggester should not propose priority downgrades for templates outside the target criteria.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- 2026-03-10 00:15 UTC: Disabled the scheduled sla-suggester job in prod.
- 2026-03-10 00:30 UTC: Rolled back autoroute merger snapshot to 2026-03-09T21:50Z to remove applied overrides.
- Added a Grafana alert to detect >10% delta in routing SLA weights after autoroute merges.

Notes on scope and exposure:
- Change was limited to internal-support namespaces (not customer-facing).
- Root cause appears limited to the DST-aware time normalization path in sla-suggester code.
- Related dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/gzSLA/sla-routing-overview?orgId=1

investigation_notes:
Summary of investigation steps:
- Pulled logs for autoroute-merger run 2026-03-09 23:00-2026-03-10 01:00 UTC. Observed batch diffs containing priority_weight patches for 'support-queue' macros.
- Replayed suggester with identical inputs in staging; reproduced the patch when host TZ simulated as 'America/New_York' with DST flag enabled.
- Unit tests for time normalization previously covered non-boundary windows; added tests for windows that cross DST transition and midnight boundaries.
- Root cause: sla-suggester's rule parser marks rules with a 'has_dst' boolean then conversion routine applied offset based on 'has_dst' and again applied system tz conversion leading to double offset.
- Risk assessment: Medium — affects only templates that contain local wall-clock windows crossing DST and only when the autoroute batch runs during the DST transition period.
resolution_notes:
Actions taken so far:
- Job disabled, snapshot rollback applied, Grafana alert added.
Planned fix and rollout:
- PR created to fix double-application of DST offset and to add regression tests.
- Will deploy hotfix to staging and run a 48-hour dry-run of suggester with feature flag off-by-default.
- After validation, enable feature flag and slowly ramp job (canary 5% namespaces -> 25% -> full).
next_steps: Merge PR 'fix/sla-suggester-timeconv' after code review and CI passes
Run targeted integration test simulating DST transition for affected namespaces
Re-enable sla-suggester under feature flag and monitor Grafana alert for 24h
Create postmortem doc and update runbook to include explicit DST test case
slo_impact: Internal escalation latency SLOs experienced a ~20% regression for affected cohorts during the incident window; customer-facing SLOs unaffected.
